search_log: Searched “Patricia Cornwell Unnatural Exposure excerpt first chapter narrator first person,” “Unnatural Exposure Patricia Cornwell point of view first person narration,” the author site, and publisher/review domains.
Searched exact combinations of the title with “first-person,” “first person,” “narration,” and Google Books preview; opened the resulting excerpt, academic paper, and contemporary reviews.
Searched the title with epistolary, multiple narrators, alternating point of view, frame narrative, and third person; found no substantiated evidence of an alternating or framed structure.
The Hachette product page identified the correct eighth Scarpetta novel but its visible “Read Excerpt” control exposed no prose, and Google Books offered only snippet metadata.

A BookRags user answer claimed third-person limited narration; opening the page revealed no supporting evidence, so it was retained only as Tier D contrary material and rejected after comparison with primary and scholarly evidence.
person_note: Kay Scarpetta is the controlling participating narrator. Multiple input speech beats and the event passage expose narratorial “I” or “we”; dialogue and the gnomic quotation were not allowed to vote independently. The authorized opening and scholarly whole-book analysis agree on first person, with contemporary reviews corroborating Scarpetta’s voice. No credible evidence supports sustained third-person, second-person, framed, or alternating sections; the lone contrary BookRags assertion is unsupported and demonstrably inconsistent with the primary prose.
